content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

Section 19 of the Brightline MSA satisfies the WARRANTY rule at the **preferred** level:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Professional and workmanlike Services | 19.1 ("by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards") — no time limit |
| Conformance to documentation | 19.1 / 19.2 (Services and Deliverables materially conform) |
| Software conformance 12 months | 19.2 — hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term** (continuous; 12-month renewal periods per 8.2) |
| Services warranty 90 days | 19.1 (unlimited duration) plus continuous hosted conformance |
| Repair / replacement | 19.4 (prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge) |
| Refund | 19.4 (terminate affected item and refund Fees paid) |
| Compliance with law | 19.3 |
| No malicious code | 19.3 |

Key checks completed:
- **Disclaimer does not gut the warranty** — 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and expressly provides that "No disclaimer limits an express warranty… or remedy expressly provided here." No "AS IS" language exists anywhere in the document.
- **No exclusive-remedy cut-back** — 19.4 states the remedy is non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; 30.x confirms remedies are cumulative; § 21 caps liability but does not touch the warranty remedy.
- **Acceptance regime reinforces it** — 6.1–6.2 give a 15-business-day test window, free correction, and a refund after two failed cycles.

Two sub-preferred details are noted in the rationale only, not flagged: the malicious-code warranty is qualified to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," and Deliverable conformance runs 90 days rather than 12 months (immaterial given the continuous hosted-software warranty and § 6 acceptance remedies).
